package_info.package_versions: All published versions during the campaign
package_info.why_malicious: The packages are intentionally created as spam or with malicious intent, containing links to scam, malware, or referral sites. Their mass publication caused a denial of service on the npm registry and exposed users to further attacks via SEO poisoning and malicious redirection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or when viewing the package metadata, the package presents links to malicious or scam websites, leading users to visit external domains for further exploitation or scams.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages do not direct users to unrelated or scam websites. The presence of external links to known malicious or scam domains is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages use metadata fields for legitimate project information, not for advertising or redirecting to malicious sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to their own documentation or project homepage, but not to unrelated or scam domains.
key_indicators: Links to unrelated or known malicious domains in metadata
Descriptions containing referral or scam links

execution_context.file_location: index.js or main entry file (in some packages)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the code attempts to open or fetch a malicious website, potentially redirecting the user or exfiltrating data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Code that automatically opens or fetches external URLs during installation is highly suspicious, especially if the domains are known for scams or malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not perform network requests to unrelated domains during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may fetch dependencies or check for updates, but not to unrelated or scam domains.
key_indicators: Network requests to suspicious domains during install

attack_chain.action: Threat actor publishes a large number of empty or spam packages with links to malicious or scam websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users or automated systems encounter these packages via search or dependency resolution.

attack_chain.action: Users viewing package metadata or documentation are lured to visit malicious or scam websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential malware infection, referral scam, or further exploitation.

attack_chain.action: Some packages may execute code at install-time to open or fetch malicious websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Possible data exfiltration, user redirection, or further compromise.

attack_chain.action: Mass publication of these packages causes a denial of service on the npm registry.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with metadata fields (description, homepage, README) containing links to unrelated or known malicious domains
Packages that perform network requests to suspicious domains at install-time
Mass publication of empty or near-empty packages in a short time frame
file_indicators: package.json with homepage or description fields pointing to suspicious domains
README files containing scam or referral links
index.js or main entry files with code that opens or fetches external URLs
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains associated with scams, malware, or referral campaigns
Unusual spikes in requests to npm registry endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose metadata fields (description, homepage, README) contain links to known malicious or unrelated domains. Flag packages that perform network requests to suspicious domains during installation. Detect mass publication of empty or near-empty packages, and correlate with known scam or malware campaigns. Use threat intelligence to maintain an up-to-date list of malicious domains and referral links.
